newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bacob CEO Bruneel sees 30% '96 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Bacob CEO Bruneel sees 30% '96 profit growth.

text.p: Belgian Bacob Bank 's 1996 earnings will show growth of about 30 percent, chief executive officer Dirk Bruneel said on Thursday.
"We are set to publish earnings growth similar to Paribas Bank Belgium," Bruneel told journalists at a press meeting.
Paribas Bank Belgium said on Wednesday 1996 group net profit rose by about 30 percent to 3.97 billion francs.
Bacob earned 1995 net profit of 2.24 billion francs.
"If the results of 1997 can remain at the same level as 1996, we will have done a good job," Bruneel said.
Bacob will release 1996 earnings on March 28.
Bruneel said the sharp fall of interest rates and the steepness of the yield curve in 1996 (300 basis points difference between short- and long-term yields) had been an exceptional boon for banks.
"This was an exceptional situation which I have witnessed only once in my 24-year banking career," Bruneel, 47, said.

He said that, on the one hand, banks' funding costs had fallen sharply, as investors reinvested funds from expired bank savings certificates at rates on average two full percentage points lower than their expiring paper. He said, however, that on banks' asset sides, the rate drop had come with a time lag.

"This year about 30 percent of our mortgage activity has been coming from refinancings of existing mortgages at lower rates. But it took lenders a while before they realised they could do that," he said.
He also said the reasons for the sharp 1996 profit growth will not be there this year.
"The turbo-effect of falaling rates is gone now," he said.

Bruneel said that he expected that Belgium's big four banks (BBL, Generale Bank, Kredietbank and CCB) would publish double-digit profit growth for 1996, but added that much would depend how they will provision for bad loans and for the costs associated with the introduction of the single currency.
The big four are set to release earnings next month.
